rv.q: There's nothing foolish about Music Theater Works 'La Cage.' It's bright, loud, romantic, outrageous and a defiant celebration of living your life as you are, and not what others say you should be.

This is the kind of production that practically compels me to call out each of the main designers, and I'd be remiss not to mention sound designer Eric Backus and very creative props designer Hayley E. Wallenfeldt.
Cast, costumes, choreography, comedy swirl together for a dynamic musical spectacle.
This is one hot production that's not only stunning in its showmanship, but equally warm and touching in its depiction of a family who radiate love and respect for each other.

The show, under the direction of Kyle A. Dougan, is every bit as fresh, buoyant and necessary today as it was nearly 40 years ago when it made a definitive statement about gay rights and won over Broadway.
Taken as a whole, this is an enjoyable production with a good cast of show voices who are better dancers than singers.
They have taken this show to a new level for the area.
La Cage brings an outstanding night of musical theatre to the Performing Arts Center in Skokie with a few surprises throw in!

cn.t: Music Theater Works delivers a glitzy, heartfelt production that balances spectacular drag performances and gorgeous costumes with the show's warmhearted story of love and acceptance, featuring a standout turn by Ginger Minj.
